We’re thrilled to announce the launch of our Delegators Reward Program, an opportunity for you to support the WorldMapPin project while earning rewards simultaneously. This is another big step in the evolution of this great project that we all love. ### How It All Started The idea popped out during a delightful breakfast at Hivefest when @roelandp asked @detlev and @lizanomadsoul if we had a plan about rewarding our delegators. Since then, we've put a lot of thought into creating a program that not only rewards you, our amazing supporters but also strengthens the Hive ecosystem. Big thank you to @arcange for coding and testing the system for the project. ### Why a Delegators Reward Program? The program aims at rewarding anyone who delegates at least 50 HP to @worldmappin in order to give back as a thank-you for their delegation. By delegating Hive Power to @worldmappin, you become an integral part of our project, supporting the curation of daily travel content and receiving a share of the curation rewards proportional to your delegation. The @worldmappin team curates travel content daily and votes for the best English and Spanish posts. Our curation rewards are quite high as we are very active in curating quality content. Our average curation APR ranges from 9% to 11%, which our delegators will also benefit from. ### How does it work? Several other projects on HIVE reward their delegators with HIVE, HBD, or with their own tokens. At @worldmappin, we have decided to reward our delegators with Hive Power (HP). The main reasons to do so are: - We will grow together - If you were doing your own curation, you would also receive Hive Power - It is a healthy way to support the Hive Eco System. We will share 80% of our curation rewards with our delegator. The remaining will be used to grow the @worldmappin account and provide greater rewards to the talented authors we curate. *Note: for efficiency reasons, we will not distribute a reward if its amount is less than 0.005 HP. With a delegation of at least 50 HP, this should not be an issue.* ### When? Our Delegators Reward Program will start on **November 1st**! This means we will collect data on curation rewards and delegations once the day is over. Only after that our delegators will receive their rewards. [Léelo en **español** aquí](#spanish)
![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EphwvnseGpoFsqerip5DYGfvbjMnpcP2dKvEaiP5Ezhaad1uqpdt9YswSrDWH917stk.jpg) # Our goal at Worldmappin Map and Travel Community Since **the worldmappin.com map** exists we have planned to extend it for all Hive users, which means everyone can pin their post on the map and link it to the content-related community - bringing all the users and communities together in one place again the worldmappin.com map. **The Worldmappin Community** is the start of showing how that works. It always has been and will be travel-related, because our vision in this **community** has always been two things: A: Provide each traveler with their unique world map, where they can explore the world, pin their trips and memories, and dive back into the memories whenever they want with just a click. B: Give the travelers a platform to share their adventures and experiences with others, so that the whole community benefits from using the map as a travel guide to finding more information and inspiration for their next trips. As you know the curation team of @worldmappin project: @lizanomadsoul, @ybanezkim26, @lauramica, @glecerioberto, and @ninaeatshere, is checking the incoming travel posts of this community every day, curating the top content and giving the winners visibility in our Daily Travel Digest. We often get questions from our community members on what to do and not do, or how they can improve their content to get curated by our team. So we took some time within the team to write down our guidelines with all the rules and suggestions, on which you can rely when writing a travel post within the @Worldmappin community. In this post, we will go into detail about every one of them. - Thanks also to @livinguktaiwan and the rest of the @worldmappin team @detlev, @arcange, @godfish,@louis88, @rivalzzz, @masterswatch and @uniforced for your input and for the support on this. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 19.17.17.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23w3EVhVkZqLVzF3s3wB8HBA6aoHDSZnwZ4rjrPDKzQj9Gi5wqtBKyYnjq4EQXm7J79wT.png) For us, it is important, that all of you have the same knowledge and possibilities to position your content within this community following the standards of quality that we seek to ensure following our vision. ![Authorized picture by @bil.prag](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23tvkkLbUnByuUE82pY5LHSVDy7hfUmnA9fEPDvhmPzSGJBpQPekoqp9yUjqtax4CrvFY.jpeg) # Intro We love and celebrate the huge diversity in our community, representing different cultures, customs, mentalities, genders, age groups, and languages. Every traveler has his/her unique character, perception of the world, values, and strengths that make him/her the special person that we love to follow on their trips. We are very aware that with this uniqueness there comes different styles of writing, taking pictures or telling a story and that is super great! So of course, this summary is meant only as a suggestion! We love and understand that HIVE is a decentralized ecosystem, where we are all free to create content in our own individual way! However, if you share our goal and want to get support for your efforts, you may want to consider certain rules and suggestions for your future posts, that allow us to establish a standard of quality. # So let's get started! Read further and get more clear on these things on the way! ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23xoueMQMECcMBErfM1aCGiDLJkg2Y2xcvtwnRnCg7WA5SBVSsTeKdAvV1teUt7yv6q75.jpg) ## Rules for posting in the community As you may know, every community has its own rules. The rules are our most important guidelines to follow our vision and keep the quality for every one of you. If you want to be in this community you have to follow them, otherwise you will be muted at some point. Those rules have been implemented since the beginning of the project and are regularly updated. ### Rule Nr. 1. This community is only for posts included in the https://worldmappin.com map. The most important rule of our community is to pin your post to our map, because for us it's not only important that you can collect your posts on your map, but also that other travelers can benefit from your experiences. Of course, this will also give your post more exposure, as well as a chance to be featured in our daily Travel Digest 😃. There are two ways to pin your post to the map: - Include PINs from PeakD: After writing your post, click on the map icon at the bottom. It's next to “ Short preview description” and above the “Advanced” icon. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.00.51.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/Eo6SchkLfuZGRfoyFcwgv3N2WiVnFNP38U8cifkis662bFNF1j2PzpwdcYQDjD7Amhq.png) - Include PINs in the rest of the Front-ends: - Go to https://worldmappin.com/ - Find the location of your publication on the map, you can do this by scrolling the map or using the search bar. - Click on the GET CODE button and then click on the exact location of your publication: a code snippet will be generated. - Copy the code and paste it into the draft of your Hive post. Then publish it. 🙂 - The code will be invisible in your post, but a few minutes after publishing you will receive a comment informing you that your post has been added to the map. ![Bildschirmfoto 2024-10-10 um 20.01.24.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/23wgUJT7kkrRyKQsXSLrRbivrgJ18h3sPeyGJVnZFTJDV8H1Xco8EN1zcJdXtpDQrCQUo.png) ### Rule Nr. 2. English and Spanish content only. (or bi-lingual with one of the languages being English or Spanish) As we want this map to be understandable for most of our users and we are still growing. We only allow English or Spanish content for now. Of course we plan to extend this rule to more languages over time but for now only those two languages are allowed and being curated. If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language next to the English or Spanish text. ### Rule Nr. 3. Only original content, no plagiarism, no AI-generated content, no recycled content. We want to know what you experienced! See your Pictures and get shared your personal knowledge - so we can be on the trip together and follow your adventures just the way you did! So please only use information, pictures, or videos that are yours (or put the source). Plagiarism is not allowed because of obvious reasons. We know that AI is the future, it is fun and that of course it can help put more value on your post sometimes, but there are also some users out there, who are writing their posts using AI only - trying to use it only to get some payout - not to share their trip experiences with others. So for us, a mix is ok, but we will know if it is 100% AI generated and that is fully against our rules as it is also not you - and therefore not following our vision and values. Recycling old posts and pictures same as writing multiple times about the same place /the same experience is not allowed for the same reasons. ### Rule Nr. 4. Content must be about places you have personally traveled to and about your experience. We want you to explore your own map, make your own experiences and share them with the community, so they get inspired to do something like that as well! We love to be on your side when you are getting out of your comfort zone, taking on new adventures and checking out new places. So don´t just plan it theoretically - go, do it, and write about it after you experience it yourself! ### Rule Nr. 5. Worldmappin is a travel community, please post reviews of accommodations, food, and restaurants in other appropriate communities. Please avoid posting on unrelated topics. This also includes - reviews about accommodations - shopping malls - restaurants - tips & tricks on transportation unless they are only a small part of your trip and not the main topic of the post OR such a place of interest to travel to, because of historic /extra cool background. However, you can pin your posts from other communities on the map, to keep track of all your visits on https://worldmappin.com. Here are some examples (click on each image to see details): |[Actifit community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-193552/created) |[BEER community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-187719/created) |[HiveFest community](https://peakd.com/c/hive-106258/created)| |-|-|-| |
[![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://usermedia.actifit.io/D9DCB68D-D042-45C3-80E3-739DF4AE1581638640735517426688)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@ninaeatshere/actifit-ninaeatshere-20241009t182346898z)
|
[![](https://images.ecency.com/DQmbpc9YajQkcxGv9kMtTkGGXMLfq3B4WSTKiriGbKDXBXz/img_3344.jpg)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@ninaeatshere/beer-tasting-at-hivefest-split)
| [![](https://images.hive.blog/0x0/https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EoGyotE2GeJxou8KqraF6yzEnaPDAYshQ2Q4njiwdHRzCKxJCNQdauwGysDMKm9XWzx.jpeg)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@ninaeatshere/restaurant-gusar-hivefest-gala-dinner-or-engesp) | | [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/Eo2BSgYeWqHyJeFCtZdKFTZdQcDyUJUersW5YPavQEspAyECJkZbG9sjAc6m2noLD6i.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-193552/@worldmappin/wmp1728499187646)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbkj8CLsRWaYya87AmM3xbgqg1UYTcLfvycps5qRkU18MhVUwRfMvGWquhuWrVmesi.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-187719/@worldmappin/wmp1727017768292)| [![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23tHbg1MP4BtYk2Qt8dEtzJ46Ld83kwSwpzMEZVNeGrJD9ojyvgMQpVyPsqFFjQJ9HmH6.png)](https://peakd.com/hive-106258/@worldmappin/wmp1726526214980)| ### Rule Nr. 6. Penalties that happen if you don´t follow the rules If you don´t follow our community rules, you will be muted. Depending on which rule you are breaking, you get a warning and will be watched or muted right away. As the general consensus within Hive is that plagiarized content, AI-generated, spam, and recycled posts meant to farm rewards are to be muted, and users involved in those activities are to be penalized by blacklisting from further curation, here we are very strict and act right away. If you break one of the other rules you will get a friendly reminder and will be put on our watchlist. If it happens again you will be muted again. - If you are having trouble with this or you have questions on it you can get in touch with us on [Discord Channel](https://discord.gg/EGtBvSM) at any time. ![Authorized picture by @lizanomadsoul](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/lizanomadsoul/EqBbJbYvcJYiErfDBaRHrRiwc7M95b4LRZV3u1CUZwZRuQR1MDpFsiiZEcvbCSTrTqv.jpeg) ## Suggestions Congrats! You have made it through the rule jungle and are enjoying the view as all the fog should be gone by now. As a big thank you for your attention and because you are a great member of this community, we want to give you a small collection of suggestions to make your content even more exciting for others to read. Of course, those things can also help to be selected by us in the daily Traveldigest. ### Headline of the post On Hive, hundreds of posts are published every day, so it is very difficult for curators to cover all the content. The title we choose is the first piece of information we see from your work, so it is important that the title of your post is short, attractive, and related to the content you submit. There is no single way, but in terms of travel content, it is advisable to indicate the location or the name of the place you visit instead or in addition to your invitation to read the content of an adventure. It is recommended to avoid long titles, there is just no need to detail itineraries or exalt the headline, so get to the point 😎. ### Bilingual posts As we told you already in the rules section: If your native language is not English, feel free to include the original version of your writing in your native language. This helps us to verify the authenticity of the text and allows you to have a wider audience and interactions with people who also speak the same language as you. Of course, always include the English translation. When you do so, please make it visually attractive and easy to follow. As for the way to distribute the content in different languages, there are many possibilities (one language first followed by the other, translation by blocks of content or in different columns, among others) and all of them are valid, the important thing is that the way you present it allows the reader to feel comfortable when reading your content. Try to put yourself on the reader's side. As for the **title**, try to point out the languages in which it is available, no need to be redundant. Here are some examples, there can be many variations of this, but the best is to indicate only once in the sentence the presence of each language: *e.g.1 “My post headline [Eng][Esp]” e.g.2 “El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]” e.g.3 “My post headline | El título de mi post”*. ### Length of content Travel and adventure are words that by themselves open our imagination to countless stories. Remember that our goal in this community is to invite others to accompany us during the travels and serve as a guide to visit. You write about your experiences and let others know about the spots you have enjoyed the most. It is difficult to summarize them in just 300 words. Of course you can, but is it enough to make your experience the best of the day? By this, we don't mean that we write a lot just to increase volume, nor that your publications have to be full of historical/technical data obtained from other sources. What we love is for you to take us on a journey with you, with your emotions and sensations through the journey that many can make, but that has been unique for you. The moment you to tell us your own story, what particularly inspired you to talk about it, it is not difficult to reach **at least 500 words**, which could be considered as a starting point to stand out. ![Authorized gif by @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/23xVMRr2moLd8z8im7sHAq2k8EfG9PfHVPrcL9fZG5vGYtn18KNTspFHUgTZai8xPZed6.gif) ### Photos and videos This is another important feature that immediately captures the reader's attention. Choosing and highlighting your images can be crucial when promoting your publication, but you must not forget that the essence of a travel post is your story, the experience, and the anecdotes that allow you to capture those moments with which you illustrate your blog. We recommend finding a balance between photos and text. You can use as many photos as you want, but remember that these serve as backup to your story, this community is not about photography, so publishing 20 photos and 100 words, is not as interesting as a travel guide. On the other side sharing only 3 images that do not highlight that incredible journey is also not telling so much about your adventure. Therefore, a basic recommendation would be to include at least 5 photos of the environment we visited, showing the landscape, the town, or the monuments. Taking pictures of ourselves during the tour, selfies, and photos of food and lodging is super nice to see, but cannot be the main part of the audiovisual material, remember that the community is focused on the traveler's destination. Try to take care of the quality of the photographs. Lack of focus and leaning without seeking dynamism or any other form of artistic expression, end up in images that are difficult to understand. As for **the videos, regardless of the length, there is no justifying the lack of text and images** sharing our experience. Not everyone has the time to watch a whole video, the best thing is to offer the viewer both options so that we not only have video views but also invite readers to enjoy our experience. We recommend orienting the device used for recording horizontally so that it is more friendly to the eye in 3Speak. ### Sources, quotations, rights, and credits We have emphasized the importance of sharing original content, based on personal experience and according to rules 3 and 4 of the community, so it might go without saying that the text, images, and other resources used in the publication must be our own. However, for specific occasions within the post, when we share an image or video **authorized** by third parties, we must give credit to the authors and link to the source link to verify its veracity. This is not a problem if we do not base our entire article on someone else's reference, but we introduce an element to improve the story we have been sharing with others. ### Tags In any case, in Hive tags must be related to the content you are writing about. Within the community, we don't require any in particular, but #Travel will help you classify your content, making it more accessible when someone is interested in this topic. Some relevant monuments or features of the place visited are #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. If you include a language other than English, use the tag of your language of origin and some reference to travel (e.g. #Spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Authorized picture by @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Engagement Last but not least, as important as all the previous sections, the commitment of each user within the blockchain and especially in the community is fundamental. Has conseguido atravesar la jungla de reglas y estás disfrutando de la vista, ya que toda la niebla debería haberse disipado ya. Como gran agradecimiento por tu atención y porque eres un gran miembro de esta comunidad, queremos darte una pequeña colección de sugerencias para que tu contenido sea aún más emocionante de leer para los demás. Por supuesto, esas cosas también pueden ayudar a ser seleccionado por nosotros en el Traveldigest diario. ### Título del post En Hive se publican cientos de posts cada día, por lo que es muy difícil para los curadores abarcar todo el contenido. El título que elegimos es la primera información que vemos de tu trabajo, por lo que es importante que el título de tu publicación sea corto, atractivo y esté relacionado con el contenido que presentas. No hay una forma única, pero en términos de contenido de viaje, es aconsejable indicar la ubicación o el nombre del lugar que visitas en vez, o además, de tu invitación a leer el contenido de una aventura. Se recomienda evitar los títulos largos, no hace falta detallar itinerarios ni exaltar el título, así que ve al grano 😎. ### Publicaciones bilingües Como ya te dijimos en la sección de normas: Si tu lengua materna no es el inglés, no dudes en incluir la versión original de tu escrito en tu lengua de origen. Esto nos ayuda a verificar la autenticidad del texto y te permite tener una audiencia más amplia e interactuar con personas que también hablan el mismo idioma que tú. Por supuesto, incluye siempre la traducción al inglés. Cuando lo hagas, procura que sea visualmente atractivo y fácil de seguir. En cuanto a la forma de distribuir el contenido en diferentes idiomas, hay muchas posibilidades (un idioma primero seguido del otro, traducción por bloques de contenido o en diferentes columnas, entre otras) y todas son válidas, lo importante es que la forma en que lo presentes permita al lector sentirse cómodo al momento de leer tu contenido. Intenta ponerte en el lugar del lector. En cuanto al **título**, intenta señalar los idiomas en los que está disponible, no hace falta ser redundante. He aquí algunos ejemplos, puede haber muchas variantes, pero lo mejor es indicar una sola vez en la frase la presencia de cada idioma: *e. j.1 "El título de mi post [Esp][Eng]" e. j. 2 "My post headline [Eng][Esp]" e. j. 3 "El título de mi post | My post headline"*. ### Extensión del contenido Viaje y aventura son palabras que por sí solas despiertan nuestra imaginación a innumerables historias. Recuerda que nuestro objetivo en esta comunidad es invitar a otros a acompañarnos durante los viajes y servir de guía para su visita. Escribe sobre tus experiencias y da a conocer a los demás los lugares que más te han gustado. Es difícil resumirlos en sólo 300 palabras. Claro que puedes, pero ¿es suficiente para que tu experiencia sea la mejor de todas a lo largo del día? Con esto no queremos decir que escribas mucho sólo para incrementar el volumen, ni que tus publicaciones tengan que estar llenas de datos históricos/técnicos obtenidos de otras fuentes. Lo que nos encanta es que nos lleves de viaje contigo, con tus emociones y sensaciones a través del recorrido que muchos pueden hacer, pero que para ti ha sido único. En el momento en que nos cuentes tu propia historia, lo que te ha inspirado especialmente para hablar de ello, no es difícil llegar a **al menos 500 palabras**, lo que podría considerarse como un punto de partida para sobresalir. ![Gif autorizado por @ninaeatshere](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/241tQTPAaoSvjN9G5z3mBNQS3XaSMPsPBceZbR5WwdZXYC9pHGsm2VAdJwwrLX1icFiib.gif) ### Fotos y vídeos Este es otro elemento importante que capta inmediatamente la atención del lector. Elegir y destacar tus imágenes puede ser crucial a la hora de promocionar tu publicación, pero no debes olvidar que la esencia de un post de viajes es tu historia, la experiencia y las anécdotas que te permiten capturar esos momentos con los que ilustras tu blog. Te recomendamos que encuentres un equilibrio entre fotos y texto. Puedes utilizar todas las fotos que quieras, pero recuerda que éstas sirven de respaldo a tu historia, esta comunidad no es de fotografía, por lo que publicar 20 fotos y 100 palabras, no es tan interesante para una guía de viajes. Por otro lado compartir solo 3 imágenes que no resalten aquel increíble viaje tampoco está contando mucho sobre tu aventura. Por lo tanto, una recomendación básica sería incluir al menos 5 fotos del entorno que visitamos, mostrando el paisaje, el pueblo, o los monuments. Hacernos fotos durante el recorrido, selfies, fotos de la comida y el alojamiento es súper agradable de ver, pero no puede ser la parte principal del material audiovisual, recuerda que la comunidad se centra en el destino del viajero. Trata de cuidar la calidad de las fotografías. La falta de enfoque y el inclinarlas, sin buscar dinamismo o cualquier otra forma de expresión artística, acaban en imágenes difíciles de entender. En cuanto a **los vídeos, independientemente de su duración, no se justifica la falta de texto e imágenes** compartiendo nuestra experiencia. No todo el mundo tiene tiempo de ver un vídeo entero, lo mejor es ofrecer al espectador las dos opciones, para que no sólo tengamos visualizaciones del vídeo, sino que invitemos a los lectores a disfrutar de nuestra experiencia. Te recomendamos orientar el dispositivo utilizado para la grabación en horizontal, para que sea más amigable a la vista en 3Speak. ### Fuentes, citas, derechos y créditos Hemos hecho hincapié en la importancia de compartir contenido original, basado en la experiencia personal y de acuerdo con las reglas 3 y 4 de la comunidad, por lo que puede que no haga falta decir que el texto, las imágenes y otros recursos utilizados en la publicación deben ser propios. Sin embargo, en ocasiones puntuales dentro del post, cuando compartamos una imagen o vídeo **autorizado** por terceros, deberemos dar crédito a los autores y enlazar al link de la fuente para comprobar su veracidad. Esto no es un problema si no basamos todo nuestro artículo en la referencia de otra persona, sino que introducimos un elemento para mejorar la historia que hemos compartido con los demás. ### Etiquetas En todo momento, las etiquetas en Hive deben estar relacionadas con el contenido sobre el que escribes. Dentro de la comunidad, no exigimos ninguna en particular, pero #Travel te ayudará a clasificar tu contenido, haciéndolo más accesible cuando alguien se interese por este tema. Lo mismo ocurre cuando incluyes en las etiquetas la ciudad, el país o la región que estás visitando. También puedes utilizar referencias a la forma de viajar, #backpacking, #roadtrip, #solotravel, #hiking, entre otras. Algunos monumentos o características relevantes del lugar visitado son #beach, #nature, #forest, #mountain, #lake. Sólo para facilitar la búsqueda de contenidos similares, en caso de que alguien se interese por el artículo debido a esa mención concreta. En definitiva, aquí buscamos compartir nuestra pasión por viajar: #wanderlust. Si incluyes un idioma que no sea el inglés, utiliza la etiqueta de tu idioma de origen y alguna referencia a los viajes (por ejemplo, #spanish, #viajes, #senderismo #deutsch). ![Foto autorizada por @louis88](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/ninaeatshere/EpvhuUYiyc9pAWJeemu1ss6qhkNptprFMgLr5LDuNr4KGWC9YLjkQxZGjS57ReLovws.jpeg) # Compromiso Por último, tan importante como todos los apartados anteriores, es fundamental el compromiso de cada usuario dentro de la blockchain y especialmente en la comunidad. Si esperamos recibir apoyo, lo más razonable es apoyar a los creadores de contenido que hacen el mismo esfuerzo que nosotros y que dan vida a nuestro universo viajero. Ser un miembro activo de una comunidad no significa sólo publicar en ella, sino interactuar con otros usuarios en las publicaciones de la comunidad más allá de responder a los comentarios de nuestros posts. Votar, comentar y aportar opiniones son formas de apoyarnos mutuamente, compartir experiencias, ponernos en contacto, hacer nuevas amistades y, por supuesto, aprender y añadir valor real al ecosistema. Out of all the trips I’ve taken, I’ve rarely had bad weather, so I feel like I shouldn’t even complain about it. Even rain can turn into a good story if you’re with the right people, like it did when we visited Areguá in Paraguay. We knew the forecast didn’t have the best news for our day out, but we decided to take the risk anyway. It could have turned out terribly, but in the end it became an afternoon full of laughter and good food 😃.
De todos los viajes que hice, rara vez me acompañó un mal clima, por lo que siento que ni siquiera debería quejarme de esto. Hasta la lluvia puede convertirse en una buena anécdota si estás con las personas correctas, como lo fue cuando visitamos Areguá en Paraguay. Sabíamos que el pronóstico no tenía las mejores noticias para nuestro día de paseo, pero igualmente decidimos correr el riesgo. Podría haber sido todo terrible, pero al final terminó siendo una tarde en la que las risas y la comida no faltaron 😃.
--- ---
--- --- My friend Noe and I had already explored quite a bit around Asunción, so for my last full day in the neighboring country, I wanted to do something more. She suggested we visit Areguá, specifically a beach that the town has. When we checked the forecast and saw it was predicting storms, we felt a bit discouraged, but we still decided to travel the 20 km that separated us from the place—along with an Italian traveler who joined our adventure.
Mi amiga Noe y yo ya habíamos explorado bastante los alrededores de Asunción, por lo que para mi último día completo en el país vecino quería hacer algo más. Ella sugirió que visitemos Areguá, precisamente una playa que esa ciudad tiene. Cuando vimos el pronóstico que anunciaba tormenta, nos desalentamos un poco, pero igual decidimos viajar los 20 km que nos separaban del lugar, y con un viajero italiano que se unió a nuestra aventura.
---
--- As I’ve mentioned several times, everything in Paraguay felt quite cheap to us—at least to me, coming from Argentina. We took an Uber to the place, which charged us less than $10 for a ride that lasted a good 30 minutes. In my country, a trip like that could easily cost double or even more. Grateful for the good price, we arrived safely at the beach, although the clouds the forecast had warned about were already hanging over us.
Como dije varias veces, todo en Paraguay nos resultaba bastante barato, al menos a mí con los números argentinos que manejo. Nos tomamos un Uber hasta el lugar, que nos cobró menos de $10 el recorrido que duró unos buenos 30 minutos. En mi país, hacer un viaje de esos podría salirte el doble o incluso más. Agradecidos por el buen precio, llegamos sanos y salvos a la playa, aunque las nubes de las que hablaba el pronóstico ya estaban sobre nosotros.
---
--- This “beach” was actually the shore of Lake Ypacaraí, so there was no sand or anything like that—rather, it was a marshy shoreline with grass. The place was nicely set up, with street vendors and plenty of space for recreation. We only got to explore it for a short while before the storm arrived, and with strong winds blowing everything around, it forced us to leave. I think it took us longer to get there than the time we actually spent exploring the place 😂.
Esta "playa" se trataba de la costa del Lago Ypacaraí, por lo que no había arena ni nada de eso, más bien una costa pantanosa con pasto. El lugar estaba bien ambientado, con vendedores ambulantes y bastante espacio para recrearse. Llegamos a recorrer solo un poco este lugar, hasta que la tormenta se hizo presente y con un fuerte viento que volaba todo nos obligó a retirarnos. Creo que tardamos más en llegar que en lo que estuvimos viendo el lugar 😂.
---
--- As a plan B, we decided to walk toward the city center, hoping to find something else to do. We saw a few shops open, and on the map we had read about some museums, but unfortunately they weren’t open on Sundays. We wandered around in the rain for a while, until it became too heavy and we were almost forced to stop under the awning of an ice cream shop to take shelter from the water.
Como plan B, decidimos ir caminando hasta el centro de la ciudad, con la esperanza de encontrar algo más que hacer. Vimos algunos negocios abiertos, y en el mapa habíamos leído sobre unos museos, pero lamentablemente no estaban abiertos los domingos. Deambulamos un poco abajo de la lluvia, hasta que esta se volvió demasiado fuerte y casi obligadamente tuvimos que parar en el alero de una heladería a refugiarnos del agua.
---
--- A few meters from the ice cream shop, there was still a small store open, which luckily sold hot food. In the end, that was our day in Areguá: the whole afternoon sheltering from the rain, eating, and sharing travel stories with Noe and the Italian traveler. We hadn’t imagined our day would end like this, but at least we didn’t get too wet.
A pocos metros de la heladería, todavía quedaba un pequeño almacen abierto, que para nuestra suerte vendía comida caliente. Finalmente, ese fue nuestro día en Areguá: toda la tarde protegiéndonos de la lluvia, comiendo y compartiendo historias de viaje con Noe y el italiano. No imaginábamos que nuestro día iba a terminar así, pero al menos no nos mojamos tanto.
---
--- I have a friend in Buenos Aires who was born in that city (I didn’t know until he saw my Instagram story and told me). When he asked me if I liked the place, well, I didn’t have much to say. I only walked along the beach for about 15 minutes, and spent the rest of the day on the sidewalk of an ice cream shop eating empanadas, drinking tereré, and waiting for the rain to stop so we could call an Uber back to our hostel. Still, this outing was memorable—even with the bad weather. At least I can say that you can survive Areguá in the storm 😅.
En Buenos Aires tengo un amigo que nació en esa ciudad (no lo sabía hasta que vio mi historia en Instagram y me lo contó). Cuando me preguntó si me gustó el lugar, bueno, no tuve mucho que decir. Solo recorrí la playa 15 minutos y el resto del día estuve en la vereda de una heladería comiendo empanadas, tomando tereré y esperando que pare la lluvia para volver a pedir el Uber a nuestro hostel. De todas formas, este paseo fue memorable, incluso con el clima en contra: por lo menos puedo decir que se puede sobrevivir a Areguá con tormenta 😅.

​
![BİR.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZPBYbuBcnzstg7QEeebcy2mWmKTgWpiWkADrGeiHSXsN/B%C4%B0R.jpg)


Take a look at the stance of this structure, which seems to be defying the passage of time. With its powerful and imposing presence, it appears to be holding onto the traces of the past as if they were a badge of honor. The weeds sprouting from between the walls, meanwhile, reveal the structure’s harmony with nature. The name of this ancient city I came across during my Aegean tour is known as the Ancient City of Kaunos. 

>Zamana direnmeye çalışan şu yapının duruşuna bir bakın.   Etrafına yaydığı güçlü ve gösterişli duruşuyla sanki geçmişin izlerini bir onur gibi hala ayakta tutabiliyor.  Duvarların aralarından çıkan otlar ise, yapının doğayla olan  barışıklığını gözler önüne seriyor. Ege turumda karşıma çıkan bu antik kentin adı Kaunos Antik Kent olarak biliniyor. 

[//]:# (!worldmappin 36.82597 lat 28.62206 long  d3scr)

![IMG20260325174049 (1).jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXidKHHZyPqtWAcFjt9yDkyva1ooEUuvpTFKaD9rYXts3/IMG20260325174049%20(1).jpg)


Köyceğiz, one of the stops on my Aegean tour, is among the most beautiful districts of Muğla Province. One of the best-known ancient cities near Köyceğiz is the Ancient City of Kaunos. Köyceğiz is known for the lake that surrounds it in an oval shape. The ancient city is located in the village of Çandır, to the west of the Dalyan River, which connects the lake to the Mediterranean coast. Our journey, which began around the quiet, serene, and still lake of Köyceğiz, took us through the water-laced paths of Dalyan until we reached the Ancient City of Kaunos. By then, we had realized that we were not merely visiting an ancient city but were also stepping into the depths of the past. 

>Ege turu rotalarımdan biri olan Köyceğiz, Muğla ilinin en güzel ilçeleri arasında yer alıyor. Köyceğiz'e en yakın en bilinen antik kentlerinden biri de Kaunos Antik Kenti'tir. Köyceğiz, etrafını oval şeklinde kaplayan gölü ile bilinir. Gölü Akdeniz kıyısına bağlayan ve yakınında bulunan Dalyan Çayı'nın batı yönündeki Çandır Köyünde Antik Kent yer almaktadır. Köyceğiz'in sessiz sakin ve durgun duran gölün etrafından başlayan yolculuğumuz,  Dalya'nın suyla iç içe  geçmiş yollarından geçerek Kaunos Antik Kenti'ne vardığımızda, sadece antik bir kent değil, geçmiş zamanın derinliklerine doğru da yürüyeceğimizin farkına varmıştık. 

![IMG20260325180608.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWBtxDRagjiQLVk9M8TMC2SjV3q87Pcre7VeSvfpBMHVi/IMG20260325180608.jpg)

![IMG20260325164220.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmc1uLhirNUzgRZReqh2MEYXZ9wZZB8mPiVRJuyNi8ZMPL/IMG20260325164220.jpg)

![IMG20260325165837.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeVeGft6USjTjYUczSH3gTACbmvnZedzoEi4eTZEsWJG7/IMG20260325165837.jpg)

![IMG20260325173527.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXdYgsMTPtYvq3yeg5sug8YA2oRp2ywDoD7PdMpLBEfd8/IMG20260325173527.jpg)

You enter the city via a long, narrow path carefully paved with speckled stones. They probably charge an admission fee to tour the city, but since there was no one at the ticket booth, we went straight in. By the time we arrived, the rain had intensified. But this rain and the scent of the earth added a special charm to our visit. It was as if nature had awakened within the city.  The wet stones and structures looked more vibrant and brighter. The city was built on a gentle slope. Upon first entering, we came across the church known as the Palaestra Terrace. This church is a large structure made of old stones, shaped like a rectangle and featuring a total of four iron gates. There are two gates on the front of the building, and historical stone ruins have been placed in front of the gates. 

>Kentte benekli taşlarda özenle döşenmiş çokta geniş olmayan  uzun bir yoldan giriş yapılıyor. Kenti gezmek için muhtemelen ücret alıyorlar ama gişe bölümünde kimse olmadığı için direk içeri girdik. Kente geldiğimizde yağmur da şiddetini artırmıştı. Ama bu yağmur ve toprak kokusu gezimize ayrı bir güzellik katmıştı.  Sanki kenttin içinde doğa uyanmıştı.  Islanan taşlar ve yapılar daha canlı ve daha parlak görünüyordu. Kent hafif yamaca doğru kurulmuştu. İlk girişte Palaestra Terası adı verilen Kilise ile karşılaştık. Bu Kilise dikdörtgen şeklinde yapılmış toplamda dört demir kapısı olan büyük eski taşlardan yapılmış bir yapı görünümdedir. Yapının ön tarafında iki kapı ve kapının önünde de tarihi kalıntı taşlar koyulmuş. 


![IMG20260325175157.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTPQMbaSsa8u9gUxFafo1nXBZz92RGknza6mEPDJ2f8uF/IMG20260325175157.jpg)


![IMG20260325172733.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWkuYkZaDAnF7r8dCx8GpLDEBCe3qgm3QWc6rUe8kdaiq/IMG20260325172733.jpg)


![IMG20260325172823.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQpwjvMwM8iPGgiFWu6CKdbP3erf7XLiiqrpCe5rf7sj3/IMG20260325172823.jpg)

![IMG20260325173039.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQi5qs2wo3BXKNF9d2J2Kw7ZgE43NzCCreY5Mc6X7rCv5/IMG20260325173039.jpg)

![IMG20260325173329.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSoQMnsHSBfBYN1pCmDNjn8rx5sABTH9Vusp5WKVR2hPD/IMG20260325173329.jpg)

![IMG20260325172912.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRaNdBvP1uY42bbY1TUvaYGHGCsoC852G29bhAQ4WqgZb/IMG20260325172912.jpg)

![IMG20260325172909.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme11b4a6eUJYkoXPYa88eyJMdS8xomjBxaHBbyJyEygph/IMG20260325172909.jpg)

When we entered through the open iron gates of the church, which has four walls, we saw round stone structures standing on the ground to the right and left of the building. The motifs on the stone blocks resembled the cross symbols of the Christian era. The slight widening of the cross’s arms is a style frequently seen in the Byzantine period.  The geometric shapes surrounding them—including triangles and squares—likely represent decorations imbued with both aesthetic and protective meanings.  Symbols drawn on stone blocks like these are commonly found on church buildings and gravestones. The symbols and styles on the stones, now wet from the rain, have become more distinct and clearer.

>Dört duvarı olan Kilisenin açık olan demir kapılarından içeri girdiğimizde, binanın sağ ve sol tarafında yerde duran yuvarlak taşlı yapıların olduğunu gördük.  Taş blokların üzerinde yer alan motifler, hristiyanlık dönemine ait olan haç işaretlerine benziyorduu.  Haçın uçlarının hafif genişlemesi  Bizans dönemlerinde de sıkça görülen stiller arasındadır.  Etrafındaki geometrik şekiller bunlar arasında üçgenler ve kareler de var  muhtemelen hem estetik hem de koruyucu anlamlar yüklenen süslemeleri ifade ediyor.  Buna benzer taş blokların üzerine çizilen semboller genelde kilise yapılarında ve mezar taşlarında çokça görülüyor. Yağmurla birlikte ıslanan taşların üzerindeki sembol ve stiller daha belirgin ve daha net ortaya çıkmış.


![IMG20260325173359.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPCbXxD81eN7LHx9gLs9evjKPKyu4UVteVqKEWSNrEQhs/IMG20260325173359.jpg)


![IMG20260325173423.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQma8Dy61bXVSyD2ayavkLMSXTRkP63gy6gQPoXubmRDQe1/IMG20260325173423.jpg)


![IMG20260325173438.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSCRdVVduNVJyCK5eKQMHfuxZ65JePBk5QUxY5WGv7Qhq/IMG20260325173438.jpg)

![IMG20260325173409.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaZMnQYRvw6hs1noTti348m6b3MGnL6m2g62CwGYnhDsr/IMG20260325173409.jpg)


![IMG20260325173703.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQbuvwtW5ao85zqAAiDyuuP1LFtKV61Vhm6qdgxx8xWFK/IMG20260325173703.jpg)

The church consists of two identical rooms. The hall of the other room is so seamlessly integrated with nature that grasses and flowers have sprouted from between the stones and walls, establishing their own independent presence. This room is more sheltered than the other and features an area paved with closely set stones. There are hidden passages in the room with the three arched stone openings that provide access to the other rooms. Stone blocks and historical remains can be found on the floor. Similarly, daisies and grasses struggling to emerge from the ground have also sprouted from between the walls. 

>Kilise iki aynı odadan oluşuyor. Diğer odanın salonu doğa ile o kadar bütünleşmiş ki, otlar çiçekler taşların ve duvarların arasından çıkarak kendi bağımsızlıklarını kurmuşlar.  Bu oda diğerine göre daha korunaklı ve sık taşlarını döşendiği bir alanlan oluşuyor. Kapalı üç kemer taşın bulunduğu odadan diğer odalara geçiş imkanını sağlayan gizli bölümlerde var. Yerlerde yine taş bloklar tarihi kalıntılar bulunuyor. Aynı şekilde toprağın üstünde yeni yeni çıkmaya çalışan papatya çiçekleri ve otlar da duvarların arasından fırlamışlar. 


![IMG20260325175016.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWdudvWv4hkHetSELd6E8bTVboHqaWseE982hvtiCugWb/IMG20260325175016.jpg)


![IMG20260325175204.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT5HzmvqiHXBmUS2US3v4Se4fK9aWcUPy5AW3tis634ks/IMG20260325175204.jpg)


![IMG20260325174955.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfPY5eYupDwtNF96MT5wX4HnJCnSAnN23ZoUH5Gedi39u/IMG20260325174955.jpg)


![IMG20260325174924.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQxTo2VUZy6oS6tTyqyygZbfTU1VtfrbsM11egALxa1Qn/IMG20260325174924.jpg)


![IMG20260325174938.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQufHLNUAuR1Ax6CZbrihj8v7o4mBvTK5KJhrvwmWzJEC/IMG20260325174938.jpg)

We can see several structures surrounding the church. While the damaged buildings struggle to remain standing, the historical ruins scattered across the grass and the symbols on them bring the traces of the past to light.  As you walk between the stone walls, you feel as though time has paused here to rest. The small flowers and grasses sprouting atop the walls look so beautiful in the rain that we bear witness to moments where nature and history converge. 

>Kilisenin etrafından birkaç yapının olduğunu görüyoruz. Hasar gören yapılar ayakta durmaya çalışırken, çimenlerin üzerinde yer alan tarihi kalıntılar ve bu kalıntıların üzerindeki semboller geçmişin izlerini gün yüzüne çıkarıyor.  Taş duvarların arasında yürürken zamanın burada durup dinlendiğini hissediyorsunuz.  Duvarların üstünde küçük küçük filizlenen çiçekler ve otlar yağmurla birlikte o kadar güzel görünüyor ki; doğa ile tarihin birleştiği anlara tanıklık ediyoruz. 


![IMG20260325174213.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmNmAXMeus5A63vCc4r9aC3irxoKfB35hjw1cfMRim2mqD/IMG20260325174213.jpg)


![IMG20260325174216.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWPPdP56UUT2hD4FMwxdH5zxtJoAyEC8nKRiS5junSVeB/IMG20260325174216.jpg)


![IMG20260325174225.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQs4b9BjwiJjqEuMz8YYB3x24UsWpycBivFoTT8K3fXuq/IMG20260325174225.jpg)


![IMG20260325174457.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRSzKsjThZnJhDyUZDpWiQJB8AxWesD1xe5xTKYWWgkAU/IMG20260325174457.jpg)


![IMG20260325174623.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeAcXcVicASsPqsTKwc9ghFCCoSTMqf6Pgz7fY4mJHRa5/IMG20260325174623.jpg)


![IMG20260325174406.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVMZ1Mmj6CaWK3VPX9GVKLhQSkyFvUcUguxjaeYN7C8kJ/IMG20260325174406.jpg)

The gray sky and the fine rain falling gently over the city seemed to bring out its essence, its character, and its radiance even more. As I wandered through the city, the historic ruins and buildings around me seemed to come to life, carrying whispers of the past into the present and telling me a different story with every step. The weariness of the clouds and their gray hues seemed to lend the city an extra atmosphere. The raindrops falling on the buildings added a melancholic air to the historical ruins. 

>Gökyüzünün gri oluşu ve yağmur damlalarının ince ince kentin üzerine yağması kentin içini , duruşunu ve parlaklığını sanki daha da ortaya çıkarıyordu. Kentin içinde gezerken, etraftaki tarihi kalıntılar ve yapılar sanki canlanmış ve geçmişin fısıltılarını bugüne taşıyarak her adımda bana başka bir hikaye anlatıyordu. Bulutların yorgunluğu ve gri tonları kentte ekstra bir hava katmış gibi görünüyordu.  Yapıların üzerine düşen yağmur damlaları tarihi kalıntılara melankolik bir hava katmış. 


![IMG20260325173336.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYnKQJThqev53eWJuURSviWnjmY4TeBc9v7nJ8LCpZ4Nr/IMG20260325173336.jpg)


![IMG20260325173640.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVfCnXwmkYH5eHSTMSqLdjnpNCBx1gZAgjamswfQ9K99F/IMG20260325173640.jpg)



![IMG20260325173109.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWZKqdpkn3UfphEMBNmoJqR4jiR5PHof4bXGB6EiF42dy/IMG20260325173109.jpg)


![IMG20260325173201.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTYNVHa1r9yxwgBqvhanqrqH7Pj4mD2ZvYh2ZRLjqqJ9H/IMG20260325173201.jpg)


![IMG20260325173244.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTn6GQLrP3cx4q9ya5SEjc8BG3BK6TPucSpMPA6NCXB9y/IMG20260325173244.jpg)

One of the most impressive features of the ancient city of Kaunos—and the one I was most curious about—is the city’s theater. You enter the ancient theater through a large arched gateway built into the high wall.  Once you step through the gate, you climb the stone steps to see the magnificent theater stage.  At the entrance, information panels on the side walls explain the paintings, historical artifacts, and symbols from that era. 

>Kaunos Antik Kentin en etkileyici ve benim en çok merak ettiğim şekillerinden biri de kentin tiyatrosudur. Antik Tiyatroya yüksek duvarda oluşturulan büyük bir kemerli kapıdan giriliyor.  Kapıdan içeri gidiğinizde taşlı merdivenleri çıkarak o muhteşem tiyatro sahnesini görüyorsunuz.  Girişte yan duvarlarda o dönemlere ait resimleri, tarihi kalıntıları ve sembolleri açıklayan bilgi panoları yer alıyor. 


![IMG20260325174308.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmR7RWW4ZgnzNVzLiUiHQnYrwpkZs6NWnt1ziShP7QK4L2/IMG20260325174308.jpg)

![IMG20260325173804.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQme83PD3uuCtoMoz6KsaKH8njWbW2d5xA6QKUYHfhwr6uT/IMG20260325173804.jpg)

![IMG20260325174009.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSTTNFo3Gi82BfaXNX7V8R8rmtybnPiWSwtrY5xqZLCiz/IMG20260325174009.jpg)

The first thing that caught my eye when I saw the theater was the daisy flowers adorning the spaces between the semi-circular seating tiers. They were so beautifully arranged between the tiers that they seemed to have become one with the history of the past. This semi-circular theater layout is found in most ancient cities in Turkey. This layout generally reflects the architectural influences of the Hellenistic and Roman periods. It was likely designed to allow the audience to see the stage more comfortably. Here, the green grass and flowers sprouting from between the stones and steps, along with the olive tree rising in the center, have infused the structure with a completely different spirit.  It’s as if they’ve become the indispensable spectators of the plays performed here over the centuries. 


>Tiyatroyu gördüğüm de ilk dikkat çeken şey yarim daire şeklinde yükselen oturma basamaklarının aralarını süsleyen papatya çiçekleri oldu.  Oturma basamaklarının aralarına o kadar güzel yerleşmişler ki;  sanki geçmiş tarihle  bir bütün haline gelmişler.  Bu yarim daire şeklindeki tiyatro düzeni Türkiye'de bulunan çoğu antik kentte yer alıyor. Bu düzen genelde Helenistik ve Roma Döneminin mimari yansımalarını işaret ediyor. Bu düzen muhtemelen seyircilerin sahneyi daha rahat görebilmesi için yapılmış. Burada taşların ve basamakların arasından çıkan yeşil otlar ve çiçeklerle ortada yükselen zeytin ağacı, yapıya bambaşka bir ruh katmış.  Sanki yüzyılar boyunca sahnelenen oyunların vazgeçilmez seyircileri haline gelmişler. 


![IMG20260325173901.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSb9SiGTCXLUmJThRD5qPtBpv6CCJTdikGS4TVeBdPoao/IMG20260325173901.jpg)


![IMG20260325173906.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmarwYPZdUXFz1kFkfKjqEyn2jPDDCYcmg8gNebK5ArjXM/IMG20260325173906.jpg)


![IMG20260325173909.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX2hFSujVadVhCnjb2WXXRXx1JDKe32VZPA2eET2azMR5/IMG20260325173909.jpg)

The theater is situated in a truly beautiful location. It is built on a natural slope, perched at a vantage point overlooking the landscape. Entry is through arched doorways formed in certain sections of the seating steps. Although the stage has suffered damage, the beauty of nature has obscured this ruin. 

>Tiyatronun konumu oldukça güzel ayarlanmış. Tiyatro doğal bir yamaca yaslanmış manzaraya hakim bir noktaya kurulmuş.  Oturma basamaklarının belirli bölümlerinde kemer şeklinde oluşturulan kapılardan giriş yapılıyor. Sahne her ne kadar hasar görmüş olsada doğanın güzelliği bir bu çöküntünün üzerini kapatmış. 


![IMG20260325173912.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPQJk45p2ghZ9q79gwspnryqwwuYx179FcvKn3er2uwsk/IMG20260325173912.jpg)


![IMG20260325173924.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeVQp3QaonPa8RtfqNxPj3e33UgyKN4AtDaFwRJ2SuyaZ/IMG20260325173924.jpg)


![IMG20260325173930.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmV8M4xW5hZfuPtBnHhUP2QtUDpg1GgeDbZg4Zwfnvcs9R/IMG20260325173930.jpg)

The ancient city of Kaunos was very different from any other ancient city I’ve visited so far. The theater area, in particular, truly captivated me. Because this city wasn’t isolated. The beauty of nature—the trees, flowers, and grasses—had clung tightly to it, become one with it, and seemed to be an integral part of its spirit and its past.  

>Kaunos Antik Kent,şimdiki kadar gezdiğim antik kentlerden çok farklıydı. Özellikle tiyatro alanı beni gerçekten çok büyüledi. Çünkü bu kent yalnız değildi. Doğanın güzellikleri ağaçları, çiçekleri ve otları, ona sımsıkı tutunmuş, onunla bütünleşmiş ve adeta ruhunun ve geçmişin bir parçası olmuştu.  


![Passenger777.gif](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRJC4twuaVWbv36cmAFG8Gc1LTcYxXa4qaoW3kqzgJRx8/Passenger777.gif)

My recent trip to Italy didn't exactly start well. Here's my bad and good expectations of Naples, Italy. ![1000054180.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/243zbSMR1yHGHZPQD9KqKVdJK8s5Nv3NG8bZZAu8XssE69SDVgKCMM8p1CKwHtuENACeW.jpg) Ten minutes after we were due to land, the captain announced that due to thunderstorms, he had tried, but was unable to land in Naples. We were now on our way to Rome, some 250km away. An hour later we arrived at Rome. They were figuring out what to do next. The options were to either take us by bus, or fly back to Naples. If we still couldn't land in Naples because of the thunderstorm, we had to fly back to Rome and by that time, we may not be able to land in Rome due to the night time curfew. It was already 11pm and we were kept on board. People were getting very agitated especially when we found out other planes landed Naples when we couldn't. The captain blamed it on lightning which happens very quick. He was essentially closing the door for potential compensation claims. ![1000054198.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23vi25jAxteA6XKdChPMExnHsoBqs8QjpK2ofaKF3Rt3vStADhDT3mYnttxjdg6Lf1JTT.jpg) Eventually they decided on the first option - bus. By the time we passed border control, it was past midnight. A handful of us had to wait for our luggage, and that took another two hours. We have no idea what was happening and the ground staff couldn't give us an answer. I'm sure it would be much quicker to go out to the plane and get it ourselves!!!. But everyone was so tired and hungry. Luckily there was a vending machine and I managed to grab a few sandwiches. By the time we left at 2am, thid vending machine was totally empty. ![1000054197.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EokWr51nS1NewCC2WC471d2uuT9LJwsDHZpoZ7hsAmtKYAGGJW2P3VcZY2xZVbvDeMA.jpg) Finally, we got on the bus and arrived at Naples airport at 5am!!! What an eventful way to start our holiday --- ### Deep fried pizza After a few hours sleep it was time to get some proper food. Naples is the birthplace of pizza, we have to start with that, but not the traditional pizza as we know. We went for a fried pizza, which was delicious. Or maybe we were still recovering from last night's ordeal.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EonkRgMd9aczFPsyjR4BLK49BQU52jZwyhowxh3yE8VJSQs4MVy29VEU86j48bULJNR.jpg
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23wMabRi3nwwtED64XYVgndYQCvvi5WmuT681VeMiKeDCuU9gGgSQTUtbBvLUWp6gp5jh.jpg https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23z7NW7o3FMNPhBsLugef8JkZKK4vFWaFJbqBmNPeeXWn8Za68jN37EtAa9vjzEbtTZ8E.jpg
--- ### Maradona Naples is also famous for Maradona. He's treated like god here, or is the city milking his connection? There's a fine line. You can see his murals everywhere, and they even have a special shrine for him at Quartieri Spagnoli. It's a little trek, and after all the effort to get there I made sure to leave a Worldmappin Hive pin behind.
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpzygSNTTNYcg21gctgaeWCkC9yCC9Jvmx6tztLGVd9Ho9j8MPch7Wv7VJCfFy7RvK9.jpg
https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/Ep3duNTLger7ACfbdvzV5rJfmc4Lk9NE2zUASAxtCigjG35ZD9Re68p7J1wd3ZjQrCX.jpg
![1000054372.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/23xVEbg8QNhkxEoSMBtskaPbC5e8Vw4ebc3w3yYYSQYW1We5v4kJB1MwCJjHBEXgTPJnj.jpg) During our stay, we visited some typical touristy spots, and went for a [grand afternoon tea](https://peakd.com/hive-152524/@livinguktaiwan/the-gran-caffe-gambrinus-in-naples-and-all-the-queues). |We wandered around the alleyways in the old town |kept on drifting back to the jaw dropping Galleria Umberto I | |-|-| |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EoEpY14vS4PaT4aWXTcRvvo8csWQKtCwRcd1udusiuoRWY3TKC9b628VUk188hYJ5u4.jpg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EogLLgzEJJqkLvXD9iZcPuNHLvUcerxy2a7dFnBkNnGwbghStsbRzLe4718cCYPdaug.jpg| |strolled along the seafront looking out to Sorrento and Capri|and when I was tired, took solace in the Basilica| |https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EqhNNBqQdXVhJXJQmcDk5GkQL3CfaBnkhYpJs6ZwY2ryxtAKCHRnmz9hTpg8oh2NcNm.jpg|https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EpGQJkpCGEE7wu9vQRdBs21ig4doAsYaeA5J5JQiwDvtoJeo2AwbrkWq7GRX1tfuWD7.jpg| My eyes wandered up to the dome as I was resting inside the basilica. And it really bugged me. I get 7, 7 days in a week? But why 32? Where does 32 fit in our life? Is this supposed to make us think about the greater universe? Can anyone enlighten me please? ### Napoli Sotterranea One of the must go, in my opinion is the Napoli Sotterranea, but only if you're not claustrophobic. And if you do go, make sure to [book in advance](https://www.napolisotterranea.org/en/). ![1000054712.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/livinguktaiwan/EoeDyDU3xNcoadrLHDevWmRBr8NH1QScVqHdtRiF5QoWebBUGa3GRW1nKeS8BCmuHG1.jpg) Naples has an impressive underground network dating back to 300BC. The Greeks mined the volcanic sandstone called tuff because it was strong and durable, and used it to build their temples. Then the Romans dug tunnels and aqueduct to feed water to different parts of the city. And in more recent times, the underground network was used as air raid shelters during the war. And this is what's so fascinating about the tour as we're led 40m underground and walk through 2400 years of history. We walked through dark narrow conduits were only a person could just about pass through. This lead us to massive cisterns with water as clear as crystal. Ending up in chambers big enough for tens of people. I had no expectation of the tour. But fair to say, it exceeded all my expectations. Highly recommended!

Hello everyone, I hope you are doing great and have a nice spring days. In the previous post, I wrote about my last trip to Lasko, Slovenia, so in the coming days I will share some more impressive spots of this place. 
This was not my first visit to Lasko, but it was my first visit to the historical sites on the hills above this place. Every time we were there we looked at the imposing church with two domes high in the hills from the foot of the town.

![IMG_20251110_110608.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eqd6bDeC8x8cVuRu6hLezHjkvxih6YymexiwMPxp7MvejgxNcxwmbiUWTMQ4CEe5hwx.jpg)

It was the Shmichel (Šmihel) church, we learned from the locals. It is a 17th-century building constructed in the Baroque style.

![IMG_20251110_110803.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoiVi6rsT28pUXwn67znQRwNwGxxkD2VYu4mqRmn9DZWJxgwTcskJYax6PW5i9DhxFG.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110850.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpQyiLZBidoDNRJyird1Wx4ALqMu7fySRoRSqyfJLTpewb2oKCiqCNT4hPa8akyBPBk.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110810.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqUfqeQBXZE5ibjXYdf77i71bH6SYuZ17QTw8rv9ySe4DspMmyRTGyabkDfVb3Sn2b6.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110753.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EorysDb32VqJiADCFxshBP33AaQFw6EAJGEpZVfAESe6WgPUQh8Ch3pqGYGAjR5aejJ.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110835.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJZYyECY2oVMGCzEyh2BvDUVH9BZxatpkFyF8Uo16qER32vN2MHJxPj8CkeQh7f5hw.jpg)

Our visit to Shmihel (St Michael) Church in Laško started with a simple moment of curiosity. From the distance, it looked peaceful and inviting, almost like it was calling us to come closer and that was enough to make us want to climb up and see it for ourselves.

![IMG_20251110_111429.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Ep7mxYshSwtgmq9HZ4dvwaB6Qpdb5oThen8d5hwtDbpwg7oYBtDD3pe1NKFwM49xpoz.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110923.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EowECQNSqTb1hSMr3uxDTq8zvVvXndhsH8cELKasmX3GHm6AUbeGz1CfoPBKYebYK17.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110946.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqBZHjA2b2nYpQrXxPWXkciv1pq7RfBAtUr333dpJRC8dZhgbYzz6YdL6drHCp54eFo.jpg)

The walk toward the church felt like a small adventure. As we got closer, we noticed a statue standing in front of the entrance, watching over the surroundings.

![IMG_20251110_110622.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqaycN4sgZWkgW2SD9NLxtiCdMaV7wA9GbWWcZNHfjVRayXSg9VTcUXsGWUNozcKDEa.jpg)

It added a special character to the place, giving it a sense of history and quiet significance. 

![IMG_20251110_111426.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqSTczga2BcwNPYXNyUYnDD9RDkQsNpGBTZmW8uz3P3gJdV2LwD91BSAzciEES1zAMb.jpg)

The nature around was fascinating.

![IMG_20251110_110706.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EnqQiXUx8uYfaexb5WLZkXwoVDfVDSm6T4n42rYAyjNknJJbTHkpbR4MFAGSnuBY2Qg.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_110644.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqL5q1rZvLaDSESYF9JUWo2CyLCTz8pdgASCYKu3hwqZb3xbEhadWMRuhMTdw5kytbM.jpg)

I enjoyed looking into the distance, high and far, breathing in the fresh clean air.

![IMG_20251110_112657.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoTZVXC4UKPPMteHVco1PWbPXmqMmA6xi69nF1fz2oUtpG4vK9XvwJhYMpPNzsjKUkz.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_113528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoTbrvVZA2yXrCeM2BcZK9JnMFPcdNPMzWmXLy31QTvhfSLXJ9S5ptCBZSXtLrweSSo.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_113435.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqSU2bG2YmrUhdmiiC47DUC8AmAJbLZntBtFGmUGV5DMZHLStzh9Rj88xYxHe6SxetR.jpg)

Unfortunately, we didn't get the chance to see the inside of the church. The doors were locked, so we could only catch a glimpse through the keyhole. Even that tiny view sparked our imagination just enough to wonder what the full interior might look like.

![IMG_20251110_111052.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpJW8wqp7qcdpzzzv3ovbfzqY9s5goSjUREbK968yGjmXnkENwpzCdgX4HSZK5hq9zh.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111100.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EoCfdg9TFmbsy3D5xgc4toB7UeK4dQxtT9KAzVRgdQE9CeK7nBnTP3rHiV2bf52V9af.jpg)

Still, the visit didn't feel incomplete. Standing there, surrounded by nature and silence, with the town below and the hills around us, was more than enough. 

![IMG_20251110_111600.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EpNpQ52fvQb8Cj1n7DAo63B3XQPaDw2PZc8CRxEeDqFLxtbbpujedx7ebNeEs4Kq6m9.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111544.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/EqNDJncQbmsnrRG8Z8mpNjwpw2vjL3rP9K9bLa9bsyyvuptMxQsAErQv5NqG2WJjt4A.jpg)

![IMG_20251110_111609.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eokd7HJbSn9Vex513S9aNYm79nQKqzyVPuP65hTUfqKZ6ip2Yn6AVi6czH5kPSa8WVn.jpg)

Sometimes, it's not about seeing everything, but about the feeling a place leaves behind and Šmihel Church certainly left one worth remembering.

![IMG_20251110_111528.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/jelenaa/Eqd72ZRWwdcPhEhMCk9fyJeP5Cdmm8rfNK1sBcB1JB1oAwfCPzHMWUGYoJGttxUTaVB.jpg)

My kids are also happier wandering around, as if that air gave them some extra energy. We felt strong and healthy there. The locals told us that there is another church nearby, so then we headed there...

result.body:
![ ](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/EonmTy5Fi6xxnpVPd6GYb5PJdHgZYz5Zaq48Kvqs2TKaV9ZTumhzafHAabMmHJPi4du.jpg)

It is hard to get a real sense of what Pokhara is like until you actually go there yourself.

It's probably because almost all tourists stay in the touristy part of Pokhara called Lakeside. It’s a convenient and even charming part of town, but all the buildings here are new - hotels, restaurants, bars - that's good for nightlife, but boring from the point of photography.

![ ](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23uQxtpRgixYo773Y3FXDqGGXFucztEovYia2kH6is6AUpSwhmTR7vHb5Snv7yS6eLzj6.jpg)

*Pokhara [on Google.Maps](https://www.google.com/maps/@28.0594248,84.7247925,8.9z/data=!5m1!1e4?entry=ttu&g_ep=EgoyMDI2MDQwOC4wIKXMDSoASAFQAw%3D%3D)*



Photos of the recently-built streets of Lakeside are pretty much all you'll see online, even you are searching for "pokhara street photography"... So, I felt there was nothing in Pokhara except for Lakeside and just buildings between 10 and 30 years old, boring for a photographer.

Why 10-30 years? Pokhara wasn't a big place until they built the first road to it in 1968. Then, it started growing slowly raising money on the international tourism which boomed in the 1990s and beyond.

Check out the streets on Google Maps? I did it, but its street views and panoramas don’t capture the atmosphere at all... Old Pokhara is centered around the Old Pokhara Bazaar, and on Google Maps, those streets look dull.

I even thought I shouldn’t go to this Old Bazaar area... But when I got there, it turned out that Old Pokhara is actually a charming place. Sharing.

![DSC_5886.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/242DQkYF4cQFg7dcHsqv58bzVY6S67YtcGmKrbcxZV66dv5ao5sbd7bxpV9m5C7JC5VUu.JPG)

There are no old quaters in Pokhara, but a series of old buildings blended with newer houses.

![DSC_5880.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23wWyFtjvAbjkccdjf8vj5xDHTvSnYTqdqsBVbsJpkB4SU6ZcU7W8J3M6rKxUuwzSNP6t.JPG)

However, the general look of this part of the city is beautiful, with many details

![DSC_5910.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23yJG8nAeEnZd2ucdageCdCduGAh8tQU42aQyn4ym2ywMnm5UiAEKvnjTNao5zC2DarHP.JPG)

and vibes of a quiet, remote mountainous town.

![DSC_5891.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xAZe7LLpKvfDzDjhzuSCA7HsZei7VFAVtaD2EPnzLjGTsnes5ghwz69ETMM8zA5Pkqy.JPG)

The oldest buildings are plain brick houses decorated with exquisite traditional wooden carvings - windows, balconies, doors, etc.

![DSC_5887.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xpAURjSHFmx8abw4igcxX641WuhSYt7AQCe3THQApZnJr2Au9Wj9gqDksPHb2jkxPxE.JPG)

The carvings of the same style as those in Kathmandu.

![DSC_5922.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xVKSgJRUc2aHDruWgFUg3ncB4MoR6yoWDtwwWemtPopiuPJhJzX7BkqwZP79x7FUfKo.JPG)

And this tiny but charming building is Bhimsen Mandir, an 18th-century Hindu temple. I told that Pokhara is very new but I meant it's new from the point of majority of buildings. The place itself, the Pokhara valley, has served as a center of trade and craft for centuries.

![DSC_5946.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/242DLNRFHTiiVdcU2LM7WUzb5LsAYYtjLmBu9zymaWFgNeygLQavyiLJ2qxV1971ABNtH.JPG)

Keep walking further along *Ganeshman Sinha Maarga Street* to see another little Hindu temple:

![DSC_5940.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23tSd3Qe1LDJnYoeYvZJSzGex7W98mjB24UthNVvYDhu7TtctsrNbHWAB5Y8WydMsAQ9Z.JPG)

These are gates to Bhairav Temple. It's new but, of course, reflects the local traditions of art and religion.

![DSC_5927.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23y8r33yoaLi78XcY1oCMHnbWXnEhW6y5BbLZGDhy3cFvi1tLc3VXV8TcvTBcicn3BUM3.JPG)

Even if buildings aren't that old, they look nice. These ones could be built in the 1980s or 1990s.

![DSC_5936.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23yJGPFoCwG3ZMps1mJ2bUjfAVpJwcbLbaQ6VGyDSFFoa5bqP7LEiYPCzcHB5vT8JwgkQ.JPG)

The 1980s and 1990s feel like history nowadays, actually. Look at the ground floor and the awning - vintage!

In old Pokhara, you can also witness how poorer buildings of the past looked:

![DSC_5949.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23wqkiPcQg8XNZfxYkx3MTZ4HyMTr8DoB6aQaDCnfviXknkgP7HXf4vvaoywPK1wVeRVz.JPG)

Many houses that disappeared could look this way - too plain to consider them architectural heritage.

![DSC_5953.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23ywsBZ19oWStNCL432eaTupEn9MGY38Rwd7igBXasL6QHXKWqNjMJ9KqP2DnpFcTnRVc.JPG)

But ones that survived the changes over the decades look very interesting, as exhibits of a museum of the city's past.

![DSC_5941.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xefSgQcBk2txticWwCTv4JCfdTniBhM4gg6VjyJzYLoE4BZwttu7Eapp4FjAAN5RPUa.JPG)

Not a palace but much richer than the previous ones. And look at the ground floor - a simple cafe for locals - no gentrification at all.


![DSC_5896.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23w2nyQJvicnzV6hHu9oNpE9cdeJP3GebrciabYE4NaLaEY1X84WSuoBcNJPWbzh9VRD1.JPG)

Another historical building - no souvenir shops, no cafes, just a store selling grain and chips. So good.

![DSC_5952.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23y8t1iECBifgC3KXVEbhwsTzTBn1BweGAVB8DSotrqHWX1wYsvnUL7JQSgqKCpMe8HX1.JPG)

Another thing that Pokhara could avoid is the urban cancer of the 21st century - those fucking private cars... Look how neat, how clean the city looks when it is not infested with cars parked all along streets making the city look like a sick animal densely covered with ticks.

![DSC_5954.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23zGcSJCMxUHav9A8i7kPdLCEvJLEqcGRY4VqipVWtRTgpf6WBi3HwrzzzoU5ouDRHUTs.JPG)

By the way, this area is quite well equipped with infrastructure.

![DSC_5935.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xehwsgkiDujekLrhqyCrYHiTtXoS9nZeSbEjpafcdydSNRg4QGwj7GfJfLNBm7AbMtv.JPG)

For example, modern convenience stores - from this point of view, old Pakhara isn't worse than Pokhara's touristy district, Lakeside.

![DSC_5930.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xp8YSzQyNhq2t5zPNaPzLsrZAGzwUChgSJW2Z5Yp8owcbA8GFbkJUNxMmNiZUAcqWQB.JPG)

Small shops are present too, of course.

And did you notice another thing that really distinguishes Pokhara from many other Asian (especially Indian) cities? 

Quite clean streets!

![DSC_5955.JPG](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/x-rain/23xyXDKVzaWRn3BtDS4pMctTcm6UZBFkqmB84xgPeBBq2swvJ2B1zgWkkZv6NKUqn1ctp.JPG)

It's 15:30, not early morning right after street cleaners do their work... It's called culture!



*The photos were taken with a Nikkor 50mm f/1.8G on a full-frame DSLR Nikon D750 on April 11, 2026, in Pokhara, Nepal*
